procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Rooming Note
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Roomed. Vitals x1. Reviewed allergies (NKDA) and meds. Smoking daily, about a pack.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CAD/HTN/COPD f/u.

Got his first COVID shot at the regional clinic Saturday, sore arm only. Second one booked for March.
No chest pain. Breathing at baseline - winded on stairs, has to stop once going up to the second floor. Morning cough, white sputum. No fever. Using olodaterol every day.
Smoking 1 ppd. He says he thinks about quitting 'every time I see you.'

BP 130/85, HR 67, SpO2 95%.
Exam: Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs diminished, prolonged expiration. Abd soft, nontender. Ext no edema.

A/P
- CAD s/p MI: stable. No changes.
- HTN: acceptable.
- COPD: stable.
- Tobacco: counseled. Gave quitline number again. No date.
- AAA: due for vascular scan this spring - he hasn't heard from them; asked him to call.

RTC 3-4 mo.

documents.title: Immunization registry update
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pt dropped off a copy of his CDC vaccination card. Pfizer COVID-19 dose 1 2/20/21 and dose 2 3/13/21 given at regional vaccination site. Entered in immunization history; matches state registry.

documents.title: mail order
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The mail order place sent me a notice that the metoprolol and the lisinopril need a new script. Can you send it. Lyle

documents.title: RE: mail order
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Done - PCP renewed metoprolol succinate 50 mg and lisinopril 20 mg to your mail-order pharmacy, 90 days with 3 refills.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Rooming Note
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Roomed. Vitals taken. Med list reviewed with pt - no changes, no new outside meds. Tobacco: current, 1 ppd. Pt declines quitline info today.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: calves cramp when he walks.

Over the spring, started walking more now that he's vaccinated. Both calves cramp after about two blocks, makes him stop; goes away after a couple minutes standing, then he can go again. Same distance every time. Not at rest, not at night. No foot sores. No chest pain with it, he stops for the legs before the breathing.
Still hasn't called vascular surgery about the AAA scan.

BP 122/80, HR 64.
Exam: Feet without ulcers. DP and PT pulses diminished bilaterally, barely palpable. No edema. Heart RRR. Lungs diminished.

A/P
1. PAD with bilateral calf claudication, new symptom - on ASA and atorvastatin. Referral to vascular medicine for ABIs and plan. Asked them to coordinate with vascular surgery for the overdue aortic scan at the same visit.
2. Tobacco - the biggest factor here too. Counseled. Not ready.
3. CAD/HTN/COPD - unchanged.

RTC after vascular visit / AWV in Aug.

documents.title: Referral status
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Vascular medicine confirmed referral received; pt scheduled 7/28 AM. They will add the aortic ultrasound with vascular surgery the same morning. Pt notified.

reports.text:
VASCULAR LABORATORY - ABDOMINAL AORTA ULTRASOUND (vascular surgery surveillance)
Indication: AAA surveillance.
Comparison: 04/22/2020, 4.2 cm.
Fusiform infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm, maximal outer-wall diameter 4.3 cm.
reports.conclusion: Infrarenal AAA 4.3 cm (previously 4.2 cm). Continue surveillance.

documents.title: Vascular Medicine Consultation
documents.author: vascular medicine
documents.body:
VASCULAR MEDICINE CONSULTATION
Date of service: 07/28/2021
Reason for referral: bilateral calf claudication

HPI: 67-year-old man with known peripheral arterial disease, coronary disease with prior MI and PCI, and an infrarenal AAA under vascular surgery surveillance, referred for calf pain with walking. He describes a consistent cramping pain in both calves after walking more than two blocks, relieved with rest. No rest pain. No tissue loss.

Medications: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, hydrochlorothiazide 25, olodaterol.
Social: current smoker, one pack per day.

Exam: BP 142/88, HR 78. Pedal pulses diminished in both feet. Feet without ulceration.

Ankle-brachial index: 0.65 right, 0.70 left.

Aortic ultrasound in our vascular lab the same morning (vascular surgery surveillance): infrarenal AAA 4.3 cm, from 4.2 cm last year. Vascular surgery will keep him on their schedule.

Assessment: Peripheral arterial disease with bilateral intermittent claudication; ABI as above.

Recommendations:
1. Structured walking program: walk to the point of moderate calf discomfort, rest, resume, building toward 30-45 minutes most days.
2. Smoking cessation - discussed at length; this is the most important intervention for his legs and his aneurysm.
3. Continue aspirin and statin.
We will see him again as needed.

orders.order: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening

documents.title: Rooming Note
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pt roomed, vitals entered. Brought med bottles; reconciled, matches list. Smoking status updated (every day).

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, subsequent.

Vascular medicine letter reviewed: ABI 0.65 R / 0.70 L, PAD with claudication. Walking program and smoking cessation advised. Aortic scan same day 4.3 cm (from 4.2).
He has been walking most days, stops for the calves at about the same two blocks. No rest pain.
No chest pain. Breathing unchanged.

HRA: independent in all ADLs/IADLs. No falls. PHQ-2 0. 1-2 beers a week.
Tobacco 1 ppd, ~46 pk-yr.

Vitals: BP 127/81, HR 68, SpO2 93%.
Exam: Heart RRR. Lungs diminished, prolonged exp. Abd soft, pulsatile midline mass. Feet: no ulcers, pulses diminished.

Prevention:
- LDCT due (baseline 8/2020 Lung-RADS 2) - ordered.
- FIT kit given.
- COVID primary series done. Flu in fall. Shingrix still not done, he keeps forgetting at the pharmacy.

A/P
1. PAD - walking program, ASA, statin. Smoking cessation.
2. AAA 4.3 cm - vascular surgery surveillance.
3. CAD/HTN/HLD - BMP, CBC, lipids today, no changes.
4. COPD - stable.
5. Tobacco - counseled at length given legs + aorta + heart. Declines a quit date. Offered varenicline again, declined.

RTC 4 mo.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lyle - labs from your wellness visit are fine. Kidney function and potassium normal, cholesterol steady on atorvastatin. Radiology should be calling about the yearly lung CT.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING - ANNUAL
Comparison: 08/11/2020.
Lungs: Centrilobular emphysema, upper lobe predominant, similar. Right upper lobe 4 mm solid nodule, unchanged. No new nodules. No consolidation or mass.
Pleura: Normal.
Mediastinum: No adenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 2. Stable 4 mm RUL nodule. Emphysema. Annual LDCT in 12 months.

documents.title: Screening results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: LDCT 8/24: Lung-RADS 2, stable nodule, emphysema. FIT negative. Both routine yearly again. Letter mailed to pt.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu IM R deltoid. Pfizer COVID booster 0.3 mL IM L deltoid (>6 mo after dose 2, age 65+). VIS/EUA fact sheet given. Observed 15 min, no reaction.

documents.title: walking
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Is it ok to keep walking on the legs when they cramp or am I doing damage. The vascular doctor said walk till it hurts some then stop.

documents.title: RE: walking
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's exactly right - walk until the calves cramp moderately, rest until it eases, then go again. You aren't doing damage; over a few months it usually lets you go farther. Call if you get pain at rest or a sore on your foot that won't heal.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u.

Walking slowed with the cold, he walks indoors some days. Calves same, about two blocks. No angina. Breathing same as last winter, maybe a touch worse on the stairs. No fever.
Smoking 1 ppd.

Exam: Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs: diminished, prolonged exp, scattered wheeze. Feet intact.

A/P
- PAD/claudication: stable, keep walking.
- CAD s/p MI: no angina, continue.
- HTN: 127/83, ok.
- COPD: stable-ish. Continue olodaterol daily.
- Tobacco: counseled, declines.

RTC 3 mo.
